scope: Waypoint 1: implement a server-owned deterministic R8 strategic decision boundary without any Gemini call, provider dependency or runtime activation.
Produce a compact full-arena 64 by 36 ASCII battlefield with exact actor, objective and support facts, a bounded committed-voyage carrier, recent-change carrier and stable basis identity.

Prepare 8 to 12 legal complete-turn candidates including the existing deterministic fallback, exact immediate consequences, future opportunities, risks and explicit uncertainty within the six-second whole-window ceiling.
Resolve model-facing candidate IDs only through current-basis one-use server capabilities and freeze strict selected/abstention response, pending/executing/committed evidence and byte/search caps.
Verify deterministic reconstruction, paired-world projection distinctions, capability rejection, response validation and detached-projection parity with authoritative R8 execution.
Waypoint 2: add a data-only, one-call local-fake adapter with a six-second whole-window deadline, strict response validation, no retry, abort, concurrency, request-budget and circuit-breaker bounds.

Integrate the strategic boundary with the private R8 coordinator through an atomic chosen-plan and pending/executing/committed voyage record while keeping all execution authority inside the current-basis resolver.
Persist the strategy policy and at most eight strategic turns in R8 replay; reconstruct committed and final uncommitted-prefix states without a provider and reject altered or extended evidence.
Attribute player counteractions separately from system changes, preserve original continuation deadlines and accepted temporary cost, and keep deterministic fallback source attribution explicit.
Waypoint 3: integrate the exact stable gemini-3.6-flash model through direct server-only structured-output REST with low thinking, strict usage parsing and no SDK dependency.
Keep Gemini shadow proposals outside execution authority while retaining source-correct pending evidence, timing, token and frozen introductory-cost measurements for every validated provider result.

Fail external configuration closed, isolate ordinary quality runs from the provider, retain cancellation/concurrency/request-budget/circuit bounds and prevent the API key or provider endpoint from entering the client bundle.
Freeze five deterministic-baseline behavioral probes and prospective useful/valid/on-time/fallback/authority/cost thresholds before collecting real deployed shadow results.

Correct deployed shadow measurement so total time covers preparation, provider and validation, and expose only allowlisted provider failure categories without retaining provider bodies, raw exceptions or credentials.

After the first Gemini 3.6 gate, retain sanitized diagnostics in the probe artifact, measure live-equivalent planner and boundary preparation, state the 160-character output limit through supported schema descriptions, advance the changed instruction to exact prompt r2, and make the temporary-cost fixture expose an explicit committed route and delayed benefit without changing thresholds or authority.

After the corrected r2 gate, add bounded deterministic ASCII and structured after-state deltas to every candidate, remove fallback identity from the model-facing brief, independently neutralize candidate identity and presentation order while retaining private server fallback authority, advance to prompt r3 and brief r2, and apply the owner-authorized eight-second whole-window deadline.
Advance to prompt r4 with a compact shared turn-based destructible-world gameplay contract and exactly one active-mode clause derived from the selected Collect, Defend or Claim objective.

After the failed r4 Gemini reliability gate, add exact stable mistral-small-2603 as a distinct server-only mistral-shadow provider using direct Chat Completions REST, reasoning_effort=none, strict structured output, exact usage and current cost measurement.

Reuse the same r4 prompt, brief, eight-second envelope, fixed five probes and deterministic execution authority; retain explicit provider identity in replay and probe artifacts while preserving Gemini history.

After the two failed deployed Mistral operational attempts, preserve both artifacts and replace only Mistral's root-union response schema with a strict top-level object whose nullable wire fields remain subject to the existing exact selected-or-abstained server validator.

After the deployed schema correction still failed before inference, preserve the third artifact, diagnose the exact request once, and replace unsupported Mistral low reasoning with the model-supported high setting while retaining the frozen eight-second gate.

After supported high reasoning exhausted the eight-second gate and an exact accepted request consumed its full 2,048-token completion budget without a final answer, move to the only remaining supported none setting and let the unchanged usefulness thresholds determine direct-answer strategy quality.

Owner-authorized 2026-09-22 Mistral trial: restore supported high reasoning, double its completion cap to 4,096 tokens, and double the next five-probe estimated-cost acceptance ceiling to USD 0.10 while preserving the eight-second whole-window deadline and shadow authority.

After the failed v5 gate, give Mistral high reasoning a full 60-second provider window after preparation; omit explicit completion-token and response-body ceilings; remove Mistral process request, concurrency and circuit limits and five-probe p95/cost acceptance ceilings. Preserve fixed five probes, no automatic retries, strict selection validation and deterministic shadow authority; leave Gemini bounds unchanged.

After the failed v6 strategy gate, add a deterministic 64x36 ASCII-to-PNG current-battlefield rendering to Mistral's shadow input alongside all existing structured facts; keep one image, five fixed probes, server fallback authority and Gemini behavior unchanged. Record a separate visual-input version, verify image pixels and request shape locally, then run one changed-input deployed comparison.

After the failed v7 full-field image gate, replace that image with a sparse one-lane-per-candidate path sheet derived from the same detached legal-turn rollouts. Give Mistral exact ordered actor waypoints, projectile impact, active objectives, terrain-removal marks and structured after-facts while omitting the full ASCII terrain and changed-row spans from its presentation. Keep the shared brief, Gemini, replay and deterministic shadow authority unchanged; verify path fidelity and run the same five deployed probes once under a new visual-input identity.
non_goals: No Gemini SDK, API key, network call, provider adapter, prompt execution, shadow mode or live model selection in Waypoint 1.
No coordinator activation, player-visible behavior, R8 public promotion, Daily/reward/PEI change, deployment variable or external-service mutation.
No change to existing R8 physics, deterministic fallback selection, objective rules, presentation, assets or legacy runtime support.
No Sorcerers source, asset or implementation input.
No Gemini SDK, API key, network call, live model selection, environment variable, deployment mutation or provider expense in Waypoint 2.
Local Waypoint 3 implementation verification does not perform a real Gemini call, mutate Render, activate live Gemini selection, promote R8 to standard Practice/Daily or change PEI/reward behavior.
Candidate deltas report simulated after-state facts and must not invent route reachability classifications that the deterministic server has not established.
The gameplay contract must not include rules for the two objective modes the player did not select.
Local Mistral verification performs no real provider request, does not add live Mistral execution authority, mutate Render, promote R8 or change Practice, Daily, PEI or rewards.
The visual-grounding comparison adds no product art asset, client image, candidate after-state images, gameplay mechanic, reward change or provider authority.

The candidate-path presentation does not add a pathfinding oracle or claim that one-turn traces establish future route reachability. It does not change live Practice, Daily, PEI, rewards or provider authority.

reviews.details: The owner authorized a full minute for Mistral reasoning and removal of completion, probe spending and operational request ceilings. Direct review confirms only the Mistral runtime receives a 60-second provider window after deterministic preparation; Gemini keeps its prior bounds. The Mistral request omits max_tokens, accepts a larger reasoning-bearing HTTP body, and has no process-wide request budget, global concurrency ceiling or circuit breaker. Same-match deduplication, one call per decision, abort, exact response and replay validation, fixed five probes and deterministic execution authority remain. The probe runner still records latency and estimated cost but does not reject Mistral solely for either metric. The timeout probe accounting now excludes timed-out calls from on-time counts.

reviews.reviewer: primary assistant direct deployed Mistral v6 strategy review
reviews.details: The 60-second high-reasoning trial solved the prior deadline fallback failure but missed three of five scenario-specific usefulness checks. The deterministic candidate facts disprove the temporary-cost explanation: selected c07 improves objective distance by 100, removes 32 terrain cells and accepts no measured temporary cost. The preserve-option selection removes 32 terrain cells although the legal minimum is one. The information-gap reply does not mention uncertainty and does not select the deterministic fallback. These are strategy-evidence mismatches, not provider transport failures. The failed result blocks live authority and does not justify repeating the identical gate.

reviews.reviewer: primary assistant direct Mistral visual-grounding implementation review
reviews.details: A deterministic PNG encodes only the existing 64x36 server-produced ASCII projection; the image is presentation context rather than a new state or action surface. Direct review and pixel-level tests confirm stable, distinct terrain, actor and objective cells, correct dimensions and byte-deterministic output; visual inspection confirmed the entire arena is readable. The Mistral request retains the same structured brief, exact candidate after-facts, response schema, high reasoning and private deterministic fallback while adding one image plus a short legend. Gemini, live Practice/Daily, PEI and rewards are unchanged. The separate visual-input version makes the changed deployed comparison identifiable without changing the shared r4 prompt or replay contract.

reviews.reviewer: primary assistant direct deployed Mistral v7 visual-grounding review
reviews.details: The failed gate is preserved as strategy evidence, not transport acceptance. It decreased fixed-probe usefulness from v6's 2/5 to 1/5 while all five requests remained valid and the deterministic fallback retained execution authority. The temporary-cost explanation claimed movement away although c01 improved objective distance by 100; the feasible-setback decision switched to immediate coin scoring; the future-option explanation claimed route preservation while c02 removed 32 terrain cells despite a legal one-cell option; the information-gap response ignored the missing support fact. The single useful reply switched after the player destroyed the route. Lower observed p95 and estimated cost are descriptive only because the five calls were not randomized or repeated. No live Mistral promotion follows.

reviews.reviewer: primary assistant direct candidate-path presentation review
reviews.details: The new Mistral-only sheet displays one lane per legal candidate, with ordered actor waypoints, shot impact, active objectives and sparse terrain-removal marks from existing complete-turn simulations. A focused independent R8 execution test confirms every selected waypoint for a terrain-heavy candidate occurred in order and its shot impact matches authority. PNG rendering is deterministic, basis/order bound and visually inspected. The compact request retains exact actor/object/strategy/after-state facts but omits the full ASCII map and row spans; the shared Gemini brief, candidate execution, replay and deterministic shadow fallback remain unchanged. Local checks do not establish deployed provider strategy quality.

reviews.reviewer: primary assistant direct deployed Mistral v8 candidate-path review
reviews.details: The failed artifact is preserved as strategy evidence. It improved fixed-probe usefulness from v7's 1/5 to 2/5 by recovering setback continuation while preserving destroyed-route switching, but v6 also reached 2/5; five non-randomized calls cannot attribute that difference to the image. The temporary-cost proposal c01 says it accepts distance loss while its own deterministic after-facts show objective distance improvement of 100. The preserve-option proposal c02 removes 32 terrain cells despite a legal one-cell option. The information-gap proposal c07 neither acknowledges missing support nor chooses the conservative fallback. Total model input tokens increased from v7's 34,908 to 39,449, so visual simplification did not reduce token use. Provider transport and shadow authority passed; live model selection remains blocked.

reviews.reviewer: primary assistant direct v6-v8 usefulness-scoring correction
reviews.details: This cross-gate audit supersedes earlier claims in this record that the v6-v8 temporary-cost proposals failed to accept distance loss. The selected c07/c01 turns end 100 units farther from committed coin-1 (500 to 600), matching the stated cost; objectiveDistanceDelta=+100 instead measures progress toward a different nearest coin selected by targetFor. The usefulForProbe temporaryCost predicate therefore tests the wrong target and can mark correct committed-target distance loss false while rewarding movement toward the committed target when it moves away from the nearest coin. The artifacts omit provider targetId/milestoneId, so the remaining predicate cannot be reconstructed and the recorded scores stay immutable. The preserve-option rule uses minimum terrain removal without a route-reachability witness; all v6-v8 proposals chose c02 with 32 cells removed against a legal one-cell option, but actual route closure is unproved. The information-gap responses omit the missing support fact; the deterministic fallback identity is withheld from the model, leaving abstention as its actionable conservative choice. Repair passes require only repair/switch strategy, and v8's passing c07 removes 61 terrain cells where c03 ends at the same 13-unit chest distance with two removed. Continuation passes check strategy/target/milestone, not move quality. Treat 2/5, 1/5 and 2/5 as probe scores rather than calibrated strategic success rates; live authority remains blocked.

skipped_checks: Automated r4 and Mistral transport verification uses local fakes. The deployed r4 Gemini 3.6 artifact ran exactly once and failed validity, usefulness and provider-fallback thresholds; it will not be rerun unchanged.
The locally verified Mistral schema correction made no real provider request. Its next real request is the changed-input, zero-retry deployed five-probe gate after this correction is deployed.
The r3 boundary was superseded before deployment, so no r3 Gemini request or replacement five-probe artifact exists; the next deployed artifact must use r4.
Physical phone testing starts at live Gemini Practice Gate A after shadow acceptance.
Visual, performance, daily/release and retired legacy coverage are not selected for this server-only slice.

The original high-reasoning gate artifact is preserved at docs/evidence/wp-027-shadow-gate-mistral-small-4-v4/result.json; it remains failed historical evidence under the original 2,048-token and USD 0.05 contract.
residual_risks: The deployed r4 gate failed at 2/5 valid, 1/5 useful and three provider fallbacks. Live Gemini selection remains blocked until a later explicitly authorized gate demonstrates at least four valid, useful and on-time choices, no more than one provider fallback, zero authority violations, p95 at or below eight seconds and total estimated cost at or below USD 0.05.

Three provider_http_unavailable outcomes do not distinguish upstream capacity, account tier or another provider-side cause. Provider reliability must be resolved before another strategy comparison; do not attribute the failures to the free tier without additional evidence.

Candidate deltas expose deterministic resulting terrain, actor, object and committed-target facts but do not establish route reachability. The temporary-cost response claimed route preservation while selecting immediate score and distance improvement, so strategically useful continuity remains unproven.

The two valid r4 calls used 5,341 and 5,708 input tokens; one exceeds the provisional 5,500-token profiling target. Deployed preparation ranged from 1,954 to 3,374 ms and p95 remained within the eight-second ceiling, but reliability prevents acceptance.

The preserved r1 artifact remains incomplete historical evidence because it omitted diagnostics and recorded preparation as zero; the corrected r2 artifact supersedes it for current operational measurement.
The corrected r2 artifact remains failed historical evidence at 1/5 usefulness and 5,999 ms p95; it does not qualify r4 and will not be rerun unchanged.

The frozen cost estimate uses Gemini 3.6 Flash standard paid rates of USD 0.75 input and USD 3.75 output per million tokens through 2026-12-31; the free tier is free of charge, and the estimate must be reviewed if shadow operation continues under later pricing.
Local fake and transport tests prove the authority and measurement harness, not deployed Gemini or Mistral latency or multi-turn strategy quality.

The first three deployed Mistral artifacts did not reach inference. The fourth high-reasoning gate reached the model but returned no final decisions within the 2,048-token completion cap and missed the eight-second timing threshold. The owner-authorized 4,096-token high-reasoning gate also failed: three provider deadlines, two valid but strategically non-useful proposals, and 0/5 useful. Timed-out calls can incur actual cost without returned usage, so the recorded USD 0.002732 is only captured estimated cost.
Mistral Small 4 remains shadow-only. It cannot receive execution authority unless a later explicit live-mode slice follows a passing fixed five-probe gate.

The deployed v6 60-second trial removed the provider-completion failure but scored 2/5 strategic usefulness. Two replies passed continuation/switch checks; later review found that the temporary-cost failure uses distance to a different nearest coin, so it cannot establish that the model rejected the accepted cost. Terrain-preservation remains a route-unverified damage-count proxy, and the information-gap answer omitted the missing fact. P95 total decision time was 31.603 seconds, which was measured but not capped in this Mistral trial; its acceptability for live mobile play remains unproven.

The deployed v7 image trial scored 1/5 with identical fixture identities. A current-state map image alone did not resolve commitment-continuation, terrain-preservation or information-gap scores; the temporary-cost failure uses the wrong target distance and is provisional. P95 total time was 20.543 seconds and five non-randomized calls do not establish a causal latency improvement. Live Mistral authority remains blocked; no unchanged rerun is planned.

The deployed v8 candidate-path trial failed at 2/5 useful against the frozen 4/5 threshold despite 5/5 valid and on-time responses and zero authority violations. A cross-gate review found that the temporary-cost scorer compares distance to the nearest coin instead of the committed coin, so this failure label is unreliable; the model's selected turn did accept the stated committed-target distance loss. The terrain-preservation case uses damage count without a route witness, and the information-gap answer still ignored missing support. The sparse sheet is not a computed multi-turn route oracle; exact future reachability remains unknown. P95 was 15.804 seconds and captured estimated cost USD 0.010464, but five non-randomized calls do not establish a causal performance improvement. Input token use rose relative to v7. Preserve shadow-only authority and do not repeat unchanged inputs.

The fixed five-probe usefulness rubric is not yet calibrated for live-authority decisions: its temporary-cost distance target differs from the committed target, its preserve-option criterion is a terrain-count proxy, and its passing repair/continuation cases check strategy labels more strongly than candidate consequences. Existing raw artifacts and scores remain unchanged. Correct the rubric and add an explicit causal route witness before interpreting another gate's useful count as strategic reliability.
